questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Most places don't allow to rent for only one semester so it was a bit hard and also didn't help that i only rather late realized that the Sit student housing isn't given to exchange students from Scandinavia in the autumn semester.

questions.answer: I didn't receive any other than from the website and the erasmus orientation

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: That is also just me being stupid but i originally tried registering for Ph.D. courses as i didn't realize that that was what they were so make sure to check that. Other than that it was pretty smooth although a bit weird and for me stressful that you if you don't get your original courses have to choose the new courses when the teaching has already begun but that is just how they do it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Most of my courses where significantly harder than the ones i Copenhagen but the courses i took master and physics courses even though was a chemistry bachelor. I think it would have been nicer to take some easier courses that you might be a bit overqualified for so that you can focus on being on exchange rather than not failing your courses. Who really cares whether or not you get the optimal academic experience. The culture is more important

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I mean it's hard to compete with the UCPH but other than the fact that there blackboard game was very weak it was fine. The professors cared but sometimes they just didn't really know the best way to teach.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Mathematical Approximation Methods in Physics
Quantum Chemistry II
Statistical Physics
Molecular Modelling

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I especially liked SP and MoMo. MoMo was chill and SP was quite interesting. 
QM2 was also okay i would recommend reading the book but skipping it's derivations and then watching the lectures from 2021. Also be vary of the exam i thought it would be essay questions but it was actually calculation questions which kind of screwed me over. 
I was not a big fan of MAMiP. It wasn't taught that well i at least wasn't very excited about the topics. It's basically just how to solve differential equations.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I guess this depends on how cheap you are but alcohol is very expensive in Norway which for me meant that i spend significantly less on it than usual. However if you are less willing to go down on your alcohol consumption it can quickly get quite expensive. Take as much with you as you can from Denmark.
I also spend a significant amount of money on ESN trips.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: See above.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: This is really a reason to go to NTNU they have some many things for students They have all sorts of sports clubs from skiing, to dancing, to kayaking and you can borrow a bunch of sports equipment like skis and backpacks for free. They also have a bunch cabins that you can go to which are super nice and cozy and then of course their is also Samfundet which is a student run organization which host big parties, concerts, debates, champagne sundays all sorts of things. That is really something you should make use of.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The easiest way i think to meet Norwegians and not just Germans is to join one of the sports clubs. And then go to as many of the cabins as possible. Hike all day everyday.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
See above. Also Nidarosdomen is the prettiest church i think I've ever seen and i think you can get in for free on Saturdays which i would recommend. Then there's also organ music.
I would also recommend that you take advantage of the fact that you are high up north to go even further up north. Lofoten is incredibly beautiful and it is just a single train ride to Bodø and then maybe a ferry to Svolvær or whatever.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: They are very scared of alcohol but people obviously still party.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a sports club and take bachelor courses

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Norway and Denmark are pretty similar but i wouldn't say to such a degree that it was boring or anything. It's still crazy to just live in a reasonably big city with beautiful nature just right there.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I don't know

questions.answer: Take easy courses, join a sports club, prioritize being social and seeing Norway over academic stuff.
